regions.name: The Dun
regions.notes: The old hill fort on the headland: the Warden's keep, the garrison, the guns over the harbour.

regions.name: Old Town
regions.notes: The walled town on the west bank: grey stone and slate, the market, the Customs House, the chapel.

regions.name: The Quays
regions.notes: Both banks of the Marrow where it meets the sea, the mole and the beacon.

regions.name: Eastbank
regions.notes: Outside the walls across the river: warehouses, the navy yard, the ropewalk, rougher taverns.

regions.name: Outside the Walls
regions.notes: The South Gate's coach house and drovers, the Barrow Green, the roads inland and along the coast.

nodes.name: The Dun
nodes.notes: The old hill fort: a square keep inside dry-stone walls, guns on new platforms facing the sea. The Warden of Dunmarrow governs the port from here for the inland country, and the garrison lives in its yard.
A tower of the Dun.
A tower of the Dun, its gun platform over the harbour mouth.
A tower of the Dun.

nodes.name: The Dun Gate
nodes.notes: The fort's one gate, onto the Muster Yard.

nodes.name: West Gate
nodes.notes: The gate onto the coast road for Thornwick. Shut at dusk.

nodes.name: South Gate
nodes.notes: The main gate: the South Road for Tallow Cross and the Halfway Road leave from here. Shut at dusk; the coach goes before dawn.

nodes.name: The Customs House
nodes.notes: A grim stone house on the West Quay. Every ship pays the inland country's duty here, and ships from the free cities (Kalatecha and Saltmere) pay it in full; the watch and the cells are behind.

nodes.name: The Tally House
nodes.notes: Where the duties are counted and the ledgers kept, with the country's charts of the north coast. Its clerks know which captains cheat.

nodes.name: The Hiring Hall
nodes.notes: Where the Warden's contracts are posted and paid: escorts inland, wreck-salvage, and the occasional bounty.

nodes.name: The Chapel of the Drowned
nodes.notes: A low stone chapel with a slate spire, where sailors' widows light candles for the men the sea kept.

nodes.name: The Almshouse
nodes.notes: The Warden's almshouse: beds for the sick, a herb garden, and two tired healers.

nodes.name: The Tarred Herring
nodes.notes: A low-beamed sailors' inn on the West Quay, smelling of tar, smoke and fish stew.

nodes.name: Iron Row Smithy
nodes.notes: Anchors, chain and ship's ironwork, and the garrison's blades sharpened.

nodes.name: Mother Brack's
nodes.notes: Remedies for chest, cough and cold, and less said about the rest.

nodes.name: The Salt Barrel
nodes.notes: Salt beef, hard biscuit and barrels of herring for the voyage.

nodes.name: The Garrison Yard
nodes.notes: The garrison's drill yard and armoury below the Dun; their sergeant will teach a blade for a fee.

nodes.name: The Market Cross
nodes.notes: An old stone cross worn smooth. The country's proclamations are nailed to it.

nodes.name: The Wool Hall
nodes.notes: A timber market hall on stone pillars at the top of the square: wool, fish and grain from inland, weighed and taxed.

nodes.name: Marrow Chandlery
nodes.notes: Rope from the ropewalk, canvas, pitch and lanterns.

nodes.name: The Navy Yard
nodes.notes: Where the inland country builds and mends its few warships. Two are on the stocks; the Warden wants more.

nodes.name: The Ropewalk
nodes.notes: A long low shed where the rope for half the north coast is twisted.

nodes.name: Grain Store
nodes.notes: Grain from inland, waiting for ships.

nodes.name: The Net Loft
nodes.notes: Nets mended downstairs; upstairs, goods that came off ships without paying at the Customs House.

nodes.name: Mole Beacon
nodes.notes: A fire tower at the end of the Mole, lit every night and in fog.

nodes.name: Shingle Watch
nodes.notes: A watchtower on the shingle, looking east along the coast.
Moored in the river mouth.
In the Wet Dock.
At anchor outside, waiting on the tide.
Drawn up on the shingle.

nodes.name: The Coach House
nodes.notes: The coach for Tallow Cross, Halfway House and Thornwick leaves from here before dawn. Fresh horses, and a clerk who takes the fares.

nodes.name: The Drovers' Rest
nodes.notes: Cattle drovers and carters from inland, a long room and a yard full of wagons.

nodes.name: South Gate Stables
nodes.notes: Horses and mules for the inland roads.

nodes.name: The Barrow
nodes.notes: A grassy mound older than the town, ringed with standing stones. Some say a king is under it, some say worse.

shapes.name: The Northern Sea
shapes.notes: Grey water and a cold wind off it. Ships come in on the tide and anchor in the river mouth.

shapes.name: Dun Head
shapes.notes: The rocky headland the Dun stands on.

shapes.name: The Shingle
shapes.notes: A long grey shingle beach running east; boats are drawn up on it.

shapes.name: The Wet Dock
shapes.notes: A stone basin off the river, its gates kept shut at low tide so ships stay afloat.

shapes.name: The Marrow
shapes.notes: The river Marrow, slow and brown, comes down from the inland hills. Its mouth is the harbour.

shapes.name: The Mole
shapes.notes: A stone breakwater from the east bank, the beacon at its end.

shapes.name: West Quay
shapes.notes: The stone quay along the west bank: the Customs House, the fishing boats, the herring barrels.

shapes.name: East Quay
shapes.notes: The east bank's quay: the warehouses and the navy yard.

shapes.name: Marrow Bridge
shapes.notes: A stone bridge of five arches; the only way across, and the watch keeps a post at its west end.

shapes.name: High Street
shapes.notes: From the South Gate up past the market to the Dun.

shapes.name: West Street
shapes.notes: From the West Gate in to the market.

shapes.name: Bridge Street
shapes.notes: Down from the market to the bridge.

shapes.name: Quay Street
shapes.notes: Down to the quay.

shapes.name: Wardens' Walk
shapes.notes: Along under the Dun's walls to the wet dock.

shapes.name: Tanners' Row
shapes.notes: Out along the east bank: the tanneries, by the smell.

shapes.name: The South Road
shapes.notes: Inland to Tallow Cross, 87 miles, through the country's heart.

shapes.name: Halfway Road
shapes.notes: South-west to Halfway House.

shapes.name: Coast Road
shapes.notes: West along the coast to Thornwick.

shapes.name: Market Square
shapes.notes: Fish, wool, timber and grain from inland; the country's tax on every stall.

shapes.name: Muster Yard
shapes.notes: The paved yard before the Dun Gate, where the garrison drills.

shapes.name: The Dun Walls
shapes.notes: Old walls of dry stone and newer gun platforms.

shapes.name: The Town Wall
shapes.notes: Grey stone, twenty feet high.

shapes.name: The Chapel Yard
shapes.notes: Slate headstones leaning in the wind.

shapes.name: The Barrow Green
shapes.notes: A common outside the walls, and on it the old barrow mound that gave the town its name. Nobody digs there.

shapes.name: The Timber Yard
shapes.notes: Logs floated down the Marrow from the inland forests, stacked to season.

place.notes: Laid out 2026-10-16 (no picture): the old hill fort (the Dun) on its headland, the river Marrow as the harbour, the walled Old Town on the west bank, Eastbank's warehouses and navy yard across the bridge, and the coach house and the old barrow outside the South Gate. Grey stone, slate and thatch.
